'''Roberto Cingolani''' (born 23 December 1961) is an Italian physicist, academic, and manager who served as [[Minister of the Environment (Italy)|Minister for Ecological Transition]] in the [[Draghi government]] from 2021 to 2022.<ref name="Reuters">{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-italy-politics-ministers-factbox/factbox-technocrat-ministers-in-draghis-new-italian-government-idUSKBN2AC2EQ?edition-redirect=in|title=Factbox: Technocrat ministers in Draghi's new Italian government|date=13 February 2021|agency=[[Reuters]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/12/mario-draghis-new-italian-government-to-be-sworn-in-on-saturday|title=Mario Draghi's new government to be sworn in on Saturday|date=13 February 2021|work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref name="It24">{{cite web|url=https://www.italy24news.com/en/2021/02/who-is-roberto-cingolani-minister-of-ecological-transition-corriere-it.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210212230440/https://www.italy24news.com/en/2021/02/who-is-roberto-cingolani-minister-of-ecological-transition-corriere-it.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=12 February 2021|title=Who is Roberto Cingolani, Minister of Ecological Transition|date=12 February 2021|publisher=Italy 24 News}}</ref> On 10 May 2023, the board of directors of [[Leonardo (company)|Leonardo]] appointed Cingolani to the position of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and General Manager.<ref web|>{{cite web | url=https://www.leonardo.com/it/press-release-detail/-/detail/09.05.2023-leonardo-the-board-of-directors-appoints-roberto-cingolani-as-chief-executive-officer-and-general-manager-lorenzo-mariani-as-co-general-manager-and-confers-certain-powers-on-chairman-stefano-pontecorvo | title=Leonardo: Il Consiglio di Amministrazione Nomina Roberto Cingolani Amministratore Delegato e Direttore Generale, Lorenzo Mariani Condirettore Generale e Conferisce Alcune Attribuzioni al Presidente Stefano Pontecorvo }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Cingolani was born on 23 December 1961 in [[Milan]], in the [[Italian region]] of [[Lombardy]]. He spent his childhood in [[Bari]], in the [[Southern Italy]] region of [[Apulia]], where he graduated from the [[University of Bari]] in 1985 with a degree in [[physics]]. He obtained his doctorate there in November 1988, and his PhD at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]] in [[Pisa]] in 1990.<ref name="Reuters"/>

==Academic career==
From 1988 to 1991, Cingolani was a staff member of the [[Max Planck Institute]] in [[Stuttgart]], Germany, under the direction of Nobel laureate [[Klaus von Klitzing]]. He planned to move permanently to Japan to work at the [[University of Tokyo]] but returned to Italy due to the death of his father.<ref name="Reuters"/> From 1991 to 1999, Cingolani was first researcher and then associate professor of general physics at the Materials Science Department of the [[University of Salento]] (then called the University of Lecce). Between 1997 and 2000, he was a visiting professor at the University of Tokyo, then at [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] in the United States.<ref name="Reuters" />

From 2000 to 2005, Cingolani returned to the University of Salento, where he was professor of general physics at the Faculty of Engineering. There, he founded and directed the National Laboratory of Nanotechnologies in [[Lecce]].<ref name="It24"/> In 2001, Cingolani worked as an expert for the Public Prosecutor's Office of Rome, giving expert opinions on the [[Murder of Marta Russo|Marta Russo]] and [[Unabomber]] cases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.radioradicale.it/scheda/127382/201359-processo-dappello-per-lomicidio-della-studentessa-marta-russo|title=Processo d'appello per l'omicidio della studentessa Marta Russo|website =[[Radio Radicale]]|date=22 January 2001|access-date=15 February 2021}}</ref> From 2005 to 2019, Cingolani was scientific director of the [[Italian Institute of Technology]] (IIT) in [[Genoa]].<ref name="Reuters" /> In December 2015, he was awarded the Rome Science Prize. In 2016, he worked on the birth of the [[Milan Innovation District|Human Technopole]] in Milan, the project for a research institute for biology.<ref name="It24" />

==Career in the private sector==
From 2019 until 2021, Cingolani was Chief Technology and Innovation Officer at Leonardo; before this, he was scientific director at the IIT in Genoa from 2005 to 2019. In April 2019, he joined the board of directors of [[Illycaffè]]. In April 2020, he was appointed non-executive director on [[Ferrari]]'s board of directors. He resigned from the board of directors of Ferrari on 16 February 2021. On 12 April 2023, the [[Italian government]] nominated Cingolani as the next CEO of Leonardo, a partially state-owned Italian multinational company specialising in aerospace, defence, and security. Cingolani initially joined Leonardo in 2019, becoming chief technology and innovation officer and spearheading cyber and AI programs, leaving in 2021. Stefano Pontecorvo was made the new Leonardo chairman.<ref name="2023-04-12_DN">{{cite web |title=Leonardo: Il Consiglio di Amministrazione Nomina Roberto Cingolani Amministratore Delegato e Direttore Generale, Lorenzo Mariani Condirettore Generale e Conferisce Alcune Attribuzioni al Presidente Stefano Pontecorvo |url=https://www.leonardo.com/it/press-release-detail/-/detail/09.05.2023-leonardo-the-board-of-directors-appoints-roberto-cingolani-as-chief-executive-officer-and-general-manager-lorenzo-mariani-as-co-general-manager-and-confers-certain-powers-on-chairman-stefano-pontecorvo}}</ref> In an interview in May 2025, Cingolani stated that Europe would create large defence companies through [[mergers and acquisitions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ebhardt |first=Tommaso |last2=Kirchfeld |first2=Aaron |last3=Lepido |first3=Daniele |last4=Brambilla |first4=Alberto |date=16 May 2025 |title=Europe’s Big Defense Deals Will Find a Way, Leonardo Says |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-05-16/europe-defense-giants-will-take-on-us-china-rivals-says-leonardo-ceo?sref=87aWS1gD |access-date=30 July 2025 |website=Bloomberg}}</ref> 

Cingolani returned to the internal negotiations within the [[Meloni government]] on the appointments of the top management of Leonardo, [[Enel]], [[Eni]], and [[Poste Italiane]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rainews.it/articoli/2023/04/nomine-cingolani-ad-di-leonardo-descalzi-resta-alleni-allenel--cattaneo-del-fante-alle-poste-a895f136-9a5b-4a72-b2f6-f16c2f3c4e50.html |title=Partita nomine chiusa: Cingolani a Leonardo, Descalzi all'Eni, Cattaneo a Enel, Del Fante alle Poste |website=RaiNews |date=2023-04-12 |language=it |access-date=2023-04-13}}</ref> Some observed argued that Law No. 60 of 1953 (Art. 6) would make the position of managing director of a subsidiary incompatible with that of former [[member of Parliament]] for a period of one year after leaving office, as in the case of Cingolani.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.affaritaliani.it/economia/nomine-cingolani-incompatibile-con-incarico-di-ad-di-leonardo-che-tegola-849552.html|title=Nomine, Cingolani incompatibile con l'incarico di ad di Leonardo. Che tegola!|website=Affaritaliani.it|language=it}}</ref> In 2024, the Ethical Finance Foundation submitted a report on this matter to Leonardo's [[audit committee]].<ref>{{Cite web|language =it-IT|author=Coordinamento Campagne Rete Italiana Pace e Disarmo|url=https://retepacedisarmo.org/2024/leonardo-boom-di-profitti-con-le-guerre-ma-solo-spiccioli-per-lo-stato-azionista-e-i-posti-di-lavoro-calano/|title=Leonardo: boom di profitti con le guerre, ma solo "spiccioli" per lo Stato azionista. E i posti di lavoro calano|website=Rete Italiana Pace e Disarmo|date=2024-05-24|access-date=2025-09-30}}</ref>

==Political career==
After the [[Ponte Morandi collapse]] in 2018, Cingolani was selected by the [[first Conte government]] as a special commissioner for the reconstruction of the bridge; Cingolani refused this charge and suggested the name of [[Marco Bucci (politician)|Marco Bucci]], who was subsequently appointed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.genova24.it/2018/10/cingolani-iit-parla-dal-palco-della-leopolda-si-fui-contattato-per-fare-il-commissario-per-genova-206594/|title=Cingolani (Iit) parla dal palco della Leopolda: “Sì, fui contattato per fare il commissario per Genova”|trans-title=Cingolani (IIT) speaks from the stage at Leopolda: “Yes, I was contacted to be the commissioner for Genoa.”|location=Florence|date=October 20, 2018|language=it|access-date=September 30, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G9ptH41jR2M|title=Matteo Renzi with Roberto Cingolani}}</ref> On 13 February 2021, Cingolani was appointed minister for ecological transition in the [[national unity government]] led by [[Mario Draghi]].<ref name="It24" /> The newly created role took over energy matters previously shared with other ministries and combined them with the environment portfolio.<ref>Stephen Jewkes (February 14, 2021), [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSL8N2KJ0CV Italy gets green superministry as Draghi eyes EU funds] ''Reuters''.</ref> He criticized [[environmental activists]] for being too ideological in their approach and called for a slower sustainable transition.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lettig|first=Daniele|date=2021-09-02|title=Italian minister: Environmental activists worse than climate crisis
|url=https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/short_news/italian-minister-environmental-activists-worse-than-climate-crisis/|access-date=28 September 2021|website=www.euractiv.com|language=en-GB}}</ref> In turn, climate activists expressed concern over Cingolani's calls for a slower transition and his statements supporting increased use of natural gas.<ref>{{Cite web|date=17 February 2021|title=Italy creates ecological transition ministry but campaigners warn against gas support|url=https://www.climatechangenews.com/2021/02/17/italy-creates-ecological-transition-ministry-campaigners-warn-gas-support/|access-date=28 September 2021|website=Climate Home News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web
|title=Technology, Diversification and Education|url=https://www.eni.com/en-IT/scientific-research/roberto-cingolani-sustainable-technology.html|access-date=28 September 2021|website=www.eni.com}}</ref> Together with the then Foreign Minister [[Luigi Di Maio]], Cingolani appointed senior diplomat Alessandro Modiano as Italy's first-ever special envoy for climate change in January 2022.<ref>Giulio Piovaccari (15 January 2022), [https://www.reuters.com/business/cop/italy-appoints-diplomat-modiano-special-envoy-climate-change-2022-01-15/ Italy appoints diplomat Modiano as special envoy for climate change] ''Reuters''. 15 January 2022.</ref> Since leaving government office, Cingolani began to informally advising Prime Minister [[Giorgia Meloni]] on energy policy.<ref name="reuters.com">Angelo Amante and Giuseppe Fonte (15 February 20231), [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/italy-wants-new-ceo-helm-defence-group-leonardo-sources-say-2023-02-15/ Italy wants new CEO at the helm of defence group Leonardo, sources say] ''[[Reuters]]''.</ref>

==Other activities==
Since 2023, Cingolani is a member the board of directors of De Mora.<ref name="reuters.com"/>
